subject: Intermittent blank completions — result of triage and closure
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@clearwave.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearWave Platform Team <platform@clearwave.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Blank response from Redwood API (request id 78910)

Hi Diego,

We're seeing an intermittent blank completion coming back from the Redwood API this afternoon. Payloads are returning a 200 with an empty string as the generated text. We attached a screenshot and the request log (request_id=78910). This is happening across ~3 users in our staging workspace, frequency ~1-2% of requests. The call was to model: redwood/gpt-opus-2 (quantized), region: us-west-2.

Could you confirm whether this is a platform issue or something on our side? We rely on deterministic completion for a customer-facing summary flow and this is breaking the pipeline.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director of Engineering, ClearWave

Hi Alex — thanks for the report and the artifacts, that helps. Quick status/update: I can reproduce an edge-case locally with a synthetic reproduction that matches your headers 1/5000 calls, but I can't reproduce reliably against the production cluster with the request id you supplied.

To help narrow: can you confirm the exact SDK version + whether you set any custom timeout/retry middleware? Also, would you be able to share one (sanitized) example of the prompt body that produced an empty string (you can redact PII)? If not, that's okay — we'll proceed on the trace you attached.

We're going to run focused reproductions in us-west-2 and inspect the routing logs. I'll loop in our internal triage and share findings by tomorrow morning PST.

Best,

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@clearwave.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Blank response from Redwood API (request id 78910)

Hi Alex / team — final update from our side after the reproduction window and log review. Summary below and next steps.

Summary of findings:
- Reproduction: We executed 3K+ synthetic requests that mirror your SDK headers, model (redwood/gpt-opus-2), sequence lengths, and retry behavior across the us-west-2 fleet and in our repro harness. We observed zero instances of a 200 with an empty body returned from the service.
- Logs: For request_id 78910 we inspected routing and kernel logs. The inbound request reached the us-west-2 front end, was routed to a model-serving pod, and the runtime reported a generation with 0 tokens because the model emitted only an end-of-sequence marker (this is a model output behavior rather than an HTTP transport error). In other words, Redwood returned what the model produced; the transport layer was healthy.
- Possible causes on customer side: short prompts with high temperature / sampling can produce quick EOS. The SDK retry wrapper coupled with a rapid client-side retry could surface a blank-looking result if the downstream code treats an empty string as transient and performs client-side suppression.

Actions taken:
- We validated the request routing and infra (no 5xx spikes, no pod OOMs, no kernel exceptions during the window).
- We ran the same prompt across model variants and a non-quantized instance to compare behavior. The unquantized run produced non-empty text; quantized binary paths showed a slightly higher variance in token-level sampling (consistent with quantization tradeoffs).
- Filed SUP-792 (internal) to track follow-ups and a brief note for our model team to examine sampling/EOS behavior for the quantized profile of redwood/gpt-opus-2.

Conclusion / Recommendation:
- At this time we cannot attribute a platform defect — the service and network behaved as expected. The output is consistent with model-side EOS behavior in the context of short prompts + sampling settings. We recommend ClearWave:
  1) Temporarily lower sampling temperature or switch to deterministic decoding (top-p/top-k adjustments) for the summary flow.
  2) Add a client-side guard: if the completion text is empty, trigger a single controlled retry that logs the model variant and request_id (instead of suppressing).
  3) If predictable, non-empty output is required, pin to the non-quantized model variant or set a decoding mode that reduces EOS frequency.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute runbook session to test guardrails with your integration team. Happy to join and walk through the mitigation changes.

Thanks for the clear artifacts — helped speed the triage. I will keep SUP-792 open and update you if the model team surfaces a regression. Closing this thread for platform action; re-open with any new failing request ids and we'll re-prioritize.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
